title: Turns at the Telescope
titleSay: Mission four. Turns at the Telescope!

science: The Moon doesn't make its own light; it shines with light from the Sun.
As the Moon goes around the Earth, we see more or less of its sunny side, so its shape seems to change: crescent, half, nearly full, full.
It takes about a month for the Moon to go through all its shapes.
The Moon always shows the same face to the Earth.
parent.summary: There is one telescope, and everybody wants the first look at the Moon. Night by night, the friends take turns while the Moon grows from a thin crescent to full.

paths.moment: Take turns, or squeeze in all at once
options: Take turns: everyone floats back and there's room.
Squeeze: elbows and noses, and nobody sees the Moon. Someone says a small 'ow'. They say sorry and try taking turns.
Tommy first (or, with one child, that child).
Button first: it says the crescent Moon is smiling.

paths.moment: Keep looking, or give Button a turn
options: Keep looking: Button waits and its light grows dim. The looker notices and gives Button a turn.

talk: What happened when everyone squeezed in at once?
How does it feel when someone gives you a turn?
Where does the Moon's light come from?

beats.say: Tonight, something special was going to rise over the edge of the Earth.
Something round, and bright, and silvery...
The Moon!
Star Station has a little telescope by the big window. Look through it, and the Moon looks big, and close.
But first, the telescope needs a polish. {A}, can you wipe the lens? Tap it three times.
Swish, swish, swish. Sparkly clean!
{T}, can you help the stars come out? Tap anywhere!
And there, peeking over the edge of the Earth, was the Moon.
["Me first!" said {a}. "Me first!" said {t}.|"Me first!" said {a}.] "Beep first!" said Button.
And everyone floated toward the telescope at the very same time.

choice.say: {A}, there's one telescope, and [three|two] friends. What should we do?

options.label: Squeeze in
options.say: Or all squeeze in at once?

beats.say: Squish! Squash! Bonk! Everybody squeezed in at once.
There was an elbow in an ear, and a nose on the glass, and a robot arm in somebody's hair.
Nobody could see the Moon at all. Just elbows. And noses. And one very surprised robot.
"Ow," said [{t}|{a}], in a small voice.
Everyone floated back. "Sorry," said {a}. "Let's try taking turns."
"Let's take turns!" said {a}.
Everyone floated back a little. Now there was room for everybody to breathe.
{T}, can you make a happy wiggle while we decide? Tap anywhere!
But who should go first?
{t} went first, and peeked into the telescope. "Wow!"
Button went first. "Beep! The Moon is smiling at me!"
The Moon was a thin, curvy sliver. Like a smile. Like a banana!
"That's called a crescent moon," said Button.
Then, one by one, everyone had a turn.
"The Moon doesn't make its own light," said Button. "It shines with light from the Sun."
"And as the Moon goes around the Earth, we see more of its sunny side, or less. So it looks a little different, night after night."
"Let's watch the Moon every night," said {a}. "And take turns going first."
{T}, can you help the nights go by? Tap, and watch the Moon change shape!
A thin crescent. Then a half moon. Then a big, bulgy, almost-full moon.
And each night, a different friend went first.
It takes the Moon about a month to go through all its shapes, from dark, to full, and back again.
Every night, the crew drew the Moon's shape on their Moon chart.
{A}, can you help finish our Moon chart? Tap each Moon.
"The Moon isn't really growing," said Button. "We just see more of its sunny side."
And then, one night, the Moon was round, and full, and bright as a lamp.
It was [{t}'s|{a}'s] turn. [{t}|{a}] looked, and looked, and looked.
"One more look!" said [{t}|{a}].
But Button hadn't had a turn yet tonight.

options.label: Keep looking
options.say: [Let {t} keep looking?|Keep looking a little longer?]

beats.say: [{t}|{a}] kept looking. And Button waited. And waited.
Button's tummy light grew dim, and its little antenna drooped.
Then [{t}|{a}] looked up, and saw Button, waiting all alone.
"Button's turn!" said [{t}|{a}], and floated back from the telescope.
Button's tummy light glowed bright again. Button peeked in. "Beep, beep, boo! It's beautiful!"
"Button's turn!" said {a}.
Button peeked in. "Beep, beep, boo! It's beautiful!"
Button's tummy light glowed so bright, it lit up the whole Cupola.
Then Button had an idea. "Wait! The Cupola has seven windows. There's room for everyone to see the full Moon, all at once!"
So [{a}, and {t}, and Button|{a} and Button] each floated to a window.
And together, side by side, they watched the full Moon glow.
"See the dark patches?" said Button. "The Moon always shows us that same face."
{T}, can you say goodnight to the Moon? Tap anywhere!
"Let's share our Moon with Mission Control," said {a}.
Button took a picture of the full Moon. Click!
{T}, can you send the picture all the way down to Earth? Tap anywhere!
A message crackled back from Mission Control. "What a beautiful Moon! We can see it from down here, too."
People all over the world can look up, and see the very same Moon.
One Moon, for everybody to share.
"This is the best Moon ever," whispered [{t}|{a}].
"Beep," agreed Button, very softly.
One telescope. Lots of turns. And one big, bright, beautiful Moon.
